chapter: Trent's band: Texas, St. Louis and the road east
title: Playing the oil-country club at Rankin, Texas
summary: A big nightclub in the middle of the desert; the band stays in cabins with their wives.

story.theme_name: Life on the road: touring bands, buses and one-nighters
story.community_name: Life on the road: buses, trains and one-nighters

blocks.x: We played a place out in West Texas--out on the desert--that was the scariest thing in my life--called Rankin, Rankin, Texas.
They only had one place there and that was Down Store (phonetic spelling).
What were you doing down there?
We went out there--this was a big, fine nightclub out in the middle of the desert and they had to depend on the people from miles around.
That's not the Bagdad; is it? There was a place between Fort Worth, a big place called the Club Bagdad.
No, that wasn't the place; no.
You didn't play that? That was a hell of a place.
Oh, I knew him very well, he used to live in Little Rock.
No, no; this was way out west, in Rankin, Texas.
I can't imagine you playing out there.
It was. They had to build us little cabins for us to stay; we had our wives with us. I'll never forget that.
